sections.title: The letter erre
paragraphs: The letter is called (erre) /ˈɛʁi/. Its main sound appears in (rua) /ˈʁu.ɐ/, which means street. This letter makes two different sounds in European Portuguese. Both sounds are consonants. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air, such as p, s or m.

sections.title: How to say erre
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue near the soft hanging part. Push the air through that small gap. Your throat shakes because the sound is voiced. Touch your throat to feel that buzz. For the second sound, tap the tip of your tongue once on the ridge behind your upper teeth. This sound is a tap.

sections.title: Reading the letter erre
paragraphs: At the start of a word, you hear the deep back sound in (rua) /ˈʁu.ɐ/. Two of them together also make this sound in (carro) /ˈka.ʁu/. Between two vowels, one single letter makes a light quick sound in (caro) /ˈka.ɾu/. Before another consonant or at the end of a beat, you hear this same quick tap in (porta) /ˈpɔɾ.tɐ/.

sections.title: Avoiding common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not curl your tongue backward like the red sound in English. For the sound in (rua) /ˈʁu.ɐ/, keep the tongue tip down and use your throat. For the sound in (caro) /ˈka.ɾu/, do not glide. Tap the ridge behind your teeth quickly, like the middle sound of the English word water.
